question: I'm reading https://dealectric.com/aa-aaa-nimh-battery-charger-8-bay-16-bay — I'm switching my whole house to rechargeable AAs. Which batteries and which 8-bay charger should I get?
query: Deal Electric AA AAA NiMH battery charger 8 bay 16 bay product specifications

replays.text:
**My pick for a whole-house setup:** standard **Panasonic eneloop AA** batteries, paired with the **Tenergy TN162 8-bay smart charger**. The TN162 is listed for AA/AAA NiMH batteries, so it matches the eneloops; the charger page is [here](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-battery-charger/). Panasonic’s [eneloop lineup](https://www.panasonic.com/global/energy/products/eneloop/en/lineup.html) is the reference for the batteries.

I’d favor the standard eneloops over a specialty high-capacity line for a general household stock. The [Dealectric comparison](https://dealectric.com/aa-aaa-nimh-battery-charger-8-bay-16-bay) is useful if you want to compare the charger’s 8-bay options before buying.

**My pick: Tenergy Centura AAs with the Tenergy TN162 8-bay charger.** The [Centura 16-AA + TN162 bundle](https://power.tenergy.com/combo-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-charger-16-pack-centura-aa-nimh-rechargeable-batteries/) is a straightforward way to start; the charger also handles AAA NiMH/NiCd batteries. If you already have enough cells, the [TN162 charger alone](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-battery-charger/) is listed separately.

For a whole-house switch, the practical consideration is charging capacity: an 8-bay charger handles up to eight cells per round, so you’ll need to rotate larger batches. If you expect to charge more than that at once, compare it with the [16-bay option in the article you’re reading](https://dealectric.com/aa-aaa-nimh-battery-charger-8-bay-16-bay).

**My pick: Panasonic Eneloop standard AA batteries with the Tenergy TN162 8-bay smart charger.** The [TN162](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-battery-charger/) is listed for AA/AAA NiMH/NiCd cells, and Eneloop is Panasonic’s rechargeable-battery line ([lineup](https://www.panasonic.com/global/energy/products/eneloop/en/lineup.html)). For a whole house, I’d buy a generous supply of standard Eneloops rather than paying extra for a high-capacity variant you may not need.

If you’d rather start with a matched bundle, Tenergy offers the TN162 with 16 [Centura AAs](https://power.tenergy.com/combo-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-charger-16-pack-centura-aa-nimh-rechargeable-batteries/) or 16 [Premium AAs](https://power.tenergy.com/combo-tn162-8-bay-smart-aa-aaa-nimh-nicd-charger-16-aa-premium-nimh-rechargeable-batteries/). If USB-C input is a priority, consider the [Tenergy TN477U](https://power.tenergy.com/tenergy-tn477u-8-bay-aa-aaa-nimh-rechargeable-battery-charger-micro-usb-type-c-input/) instead.
